To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the engine inlet manifold and the compressor air inlet duct volume have a significant influence on the transient behavior of the engine during compressor surging.

the transient operation of a diesel engine can induce compressor surging; this form of compressor dynamic stability may be avoided by increasing the length of the air duct or by decreasing the engine inlet manifold; and the engine simulation model is a useful tool for studying the transient behavior of turbocharged diesel engine.
the transient simulation of turbocharged diesel engine operation, when compressor surging takes place, can be performed using a simple linearized quasi-steddy model.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects:
    - The development and application of a model for predicting the dynamic behavior during compressor surging of turbocharged diesel engine aircharging systems.
the development of a linearized quasi steady engine model which can predict the transient behavior of turbocharged diesel engine, including compressor surging, with reasonable accuracy.
the development and application of a simulation tool to study the transient operation of turbochargers during compressor surging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the compressor surging behavior can be predicted and controlled by means of an appropriate design of the air charging system.
the compressor surge is not a problem for the automotive diesel engine, since the surge margin is very high.
the engine manifold volume has a very significant effect on the compressor surge phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the linearized quasi-stadard analysis is capable of predicting the dynamic behavior during compressor surging and that the phenomenon of surger is strongly dependent on engine inlet manifold volume.

the transient simulation model developed in conjunction with the quasi-steady code is able to predict the dynamic behavior of turbocharged diesel engine aircharging systems when compressor surging takes place.
the transient analysis of the turbocharged aircharging system is a very useful tool for studying the phenomenon of compressor surging.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a linearized quasi steady model can be successfully applied for studying the transient behavior of turbocharged diesel engine systems during compressor surging, and it can be used for the development of engine control systems.
the compressor surging phenomenon is a function of the engine and turbocharger operating conditions and of the geometry of the engine air intake system.
the transient behavior of the engine is strongly affected by the engine inlet manifold geometry.
